question: A digital health startup wants to route protected health information (PHI) from patient intake forms through Claude to summarize clinical notes. The compliance team confirms Anthropic has signed a Business Associate Agreement (BAA) with the company, but must choose where in the Claude product surface this workflow can legally process PHI. Which deployment satisfies the BAA?
options: A) A Claude Pro subscription shared among clinical staff for quick ad hoc chart lookups during rounds
B) The Claude Console's Workbench interface, since it authenticates through the same organization as the API
C) A dedicated HIPAA-enabled organization calling the Claude API with only BAA-eligible features enabled
D) The default Claude Enterprise workspace, without activating HIPAA settings under Data & Privacy
correct_answers: C) A dedicated HIPAA-enabled organization calling the Claude API with only BAA-eligible features enabled
explanations: Claude Free, Pro, Max, and Team consumer plans are not covered under the BAA regardless of who uses them.
The Console and Workbench interfaces are explicitly excluded from HIPAA readiness even when the underlying organization has a signed BAA.
Correct. HIPAA readiness is provisioned as a dedicated HIPAA-enabled organization on the Claude API, restricted to BAA-eligible features, which is the arrangement that legally covers PHI processing.
Enterprise coverage requires an administrator to activate HIPAA-ready settings and sign the BAA; a default, unconfigured workspace is not covered.
